note: All three games ran the full 60 s. Seed 101 finished within about 7 segments of the maximum, but 202 lost about 100 segments at 30-40 s on gentle road, and 303 lost about 125 in the first 10 s (speed 0.45 at 10 s) and about 155 around 45-50 s (outer side of the long +4 curve, speed 0.47). Each of these costs about as much as one hit on a slow car or one roadside object (speed down to about 0.2), while a one-decision brake tap costs about 2 segments; v3 charged a close pass at most 3 segments, and treated going off the road beyond the 12 listed segments, or after its 3-s horizon, as if nothing stood there. The new extractor charges passes with less than 0.2 side gap in proportion to what hitting that car would cost (hard margin 0.05); it charges off-road stretches beyond the listed objects, and the rest-of-bend drift, at each side's recently seen rate of roadside objects; and it adds brake-now two-line plans and a brake-in-half-a-second plan. Fields, rules, actions and timing are unchanged; no failure windows were saved, so no regression tests could be added.
instructions: Javascript Racer: Up accelerates, Down brakes, Left/Right steer. Drive as far as possible: stay on the road (off it the car slows down and stops dead against trees and billboards), steer into the curves (they push the car outward), and pass slower cars without touching them (running into one from behind drops you below its speed). Every field describes the moment the chosen action takes effect. The perception replays the game's own physics for the next 2 s: steering, the curve's outward push, gas/brake/off-road speed changes, hitting slower cars, roadside objects, and the traffic's own lane changes (each car swerves around slower cars ahead of it). It then runs 1 s more on the road ahead with the car moving to the inside of hard bends. It forecasts each bend beyond the 30 visible segments from its measured shape (ease-in, hold, ease-out), and charges every plan for how far the rest of the bend would push the car off the road. Passing a slower car with less than 0.2 of side gap is charged in proportion to what hitting that car would cost. Roadside objects are known exactly for the next 12 segments; beyond them, running off the road on a side is charged at the rate of objects recently seen on that side. It does this for 12 target lines across the road x 10 throttle plans (brake now for 1-8 decisions, or accelerate now and possibly brake from the next decision or half a second later), plus plans that hold one line for 0.5 s and then move to another, either accelerating or braking now. openX is the first target line of the best plan. openDxSteps is how far openX is from where the car will be after one decision without steering, measured in the distance one decision of steering covers (positive: openX is to the right). keepLoss is how many road segments the best accelerate-now plan loses over the next 3 s compared with an empty straight road. slowGain is how many segments braking now gains over the best accelerate-now plan (negative: braking now would cost that many). RULES. STEERING: if openDxSteps >= 0.5 use a Right action; if openDxSteps <= -0.5 use a Left action; otherwise do not steer. THROTTLE: if slowGain >= 0.5 use a brake action (brake, brakeLeft or brakeRight); otherwise use a gas action (gas, gasLeft or gasRight). Combine the two: slowGain 1.2 with openDxSteps -0.8 gives brakeLeft; slowGain -3 with openDxSteps 0.2 gives gas; slowGain -1.7 with openDxSteps 2.4 gives gasRight. Context only: speed (0-1 of top speed), x (the car across the road, -1 left edge, 1 right edge), offRoad, curve (the bend under the car, positive to the right), lineHitMs (time until you hit a slower car if you keep this line and accelerate; 2000 means none).
